title: Elimination with Multiplying First
short: Scale one or both equations so a variable will cancel.
trouble: Students multiply only the left side of an equation, forgetting the constant on the right.

blocks.html: Often neither variable is ready to cancel: in $2x + 3y = 12$ and $5x - 2y = 11$, no coefficients match. You can make them match. This extends elimination with one extra step.

Multiplying both sides of an equation by the same nonzero number gives an equivalent equation with exactly the same solutions; it is the same line, written differently. So you may scale either equation, or both, until one variable has opposite coefficients. The least common multiple of the two coefficients tells you the smallest numbers to use.

blocks.name: linesystem
blocks.cap: The two lines cross at $(3, 2)$. Multiplying an equation by a number does not move its line, so the crossing point stays the same.

blocks.html: Pick a variable. Multiply one or both equations (every term, on both sides) so its coefficients become opposites. Add, solve, substitute back, check. If both variables cancel, $0 = 0$ means infinitely many solutions and $0 = 5$ means none.

blocks.title: Scale both equations
steps: Eliminate $y$: the coefficients $3$ and $-2$ can both become $6$ and $-6$.
First equation times $2$: $4x + 6y = 24$. Second equation times $3$: $15x - 6y = 33$.

blocks.title: Scale one equation
steps: Eliminate $x$: multiply the first equation by $-3$: $-3x - 12y = -6$.

blocks.title: When everything cancels
steps: Add to the second: $0 = 11$, which is false.
No pair $(x, y)$ makes both true: the lines are parallel.

blocks.html: Multiplying only the left side of an equation. “Times $3$” must reach the constant too: $3(5x - 2y) = 3(11)$ gives $15x - 6y = 33$, not $15x - 6y = 11$. A wrong right side moves the line and gives a wrong answer, which a check in the original equations will catch.
